description.narrative: The objective of this project is to enable the City of Mykolaiv, subsequently the city of Kremenchuk, to rehabilitate critical infrastructure in water supply and sanitation and district heating to ensure that basic municipal services are available to its citizens. Project title Mykolaiv – Denmark Partnership - Early Recovery and Reconstruction - Technical Feasibility Studies, Danida Sustainable Infrastructure Fund Project objective The objective of this engagement by the Danida Sustainable Infrastructure Fund (DSIF) is, through technical feasibilities study to: 1) Provide technical assessment of the critical needs and interventions required to re-establish critical infrastructure in the city of Mykolaiv and the city of Kremenchuk pertaining to water and heating to ensure that basic municipal services are available to its citizens during the coming winter; 2) Provide short-term technical assistance and support the longer term aims of recovering of water and DH infrastructure to build back better, cleaner and greener. 3 Outcome Increased availability of critical infrastructure in the city of Mykolaiv and the city of Kremenchuk pertaining to water and heating through provision of technical assistance provided to key Ukrainian partners. Outcome indicator Technical assistance provided to ensure access to sufficient water supply of acceptably quality standards in place to serve 85 % of pre-war population of 480.000 inhabitants in Mykolaiv and temporary heating solutions in place for the 180.000 Kremenchuk residents. Output Technical assistance and expertise provided to key Ukranian partners. Output indicator Feasibility studies developed and technical assistance provided as basis for reconstruction of critical infrastructure. Baseline Year August 2022 Damaged buildings and water and energy utilities prevent citizens from accessing basic rights and services. Detailed baseline to be established as part of the feasibility studies. Annual target Year 1 Dec 2023
